rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains believing in the good as trusting that God will repay what one gives.
rows.anchor: أي بالخلف من اللّه تعالى على عطائه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that two angels descend each morning, one asking God to recompense the spender and the other to ruin the miser.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم : ( ما من يوم يصبح العباد فيه إلا

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that at sunset two angels call for recompense for the spender and loss for the miser; the passage was revealed in connection with this.
rows.anchor: وروى من حديث أبي الدرداء : أن رسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم قال : ( ما من يوم غربت شمسه إلا بعث

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes take the giver to be someone who gives to people in hardship.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل التفسير : " فأما من أعطى " المعسرين

rows.speaker: قتاده
rows.claim: Qatada says the giver is one who gives God the due owed to Him.
rows.anchor: وقال قتاده : أعطى حق اللّه تعالى الذي عليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the giver offers truth from his heart.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : أعطى الصدق من قلبه

rows.speaker: الضحاك والسلمي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak, al-Sulami, and Ibn Abbas interpret the good as the testimony that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: قاله الضحاك والسلمي وابن عباس أيضا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the good as Paradise, citing the promise of the best reward and more.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : بالجنة . دليله قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says it means believing God's promise to reward him.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : بموعود اللّه الذي وعده أن يثيبه

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets it as believing in prayer, almsgiving, and fasting.
rows.anchor: زيد بن أسلم : بالصلاة والزكاة والصوم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes it as trusting that God will repay his giving; al-Tabari prefers this interpretation.
rows.anchor: الحسن : بالخلف من عطائه ، وهو اختيار الطبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the interpretations are close because they all return to reward, which is Paradise.
rows.anchor: إذ كله يرجع إلى الثواب الذي هو الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides the person toward causes of goodness and righteousness until doing them becomes easy.
rows.anchor: أي نرشده لأسباب الخير والصلاح ، حتى يسهل عليه فعلها

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the easy course means Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم : " لليسرى " للجنة

rows.speaker: علي عن النبي
rows.claim: Ali reports the Prophet teaching that each person's destination is recorded, yet people must act: each is facilitated toward the deeds of the fortunate or wretched. The Prophet recited this passage; al-Tirmidhi calls the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين والترمذي عن علي رضي اللّه عنه قال : كنا في جنازة بالبقيع

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Two young men ask whether deeds follow what the pens recorded or are newly determined; the Prophet says they follow what was recorded and urges them to work, since each is facilitated for what he was created to do.
rows.anchor: وسأل غلامان شابان رسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم فقالا : العمل فيما جفت به الأقلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser clings to what he has and gives no good; his worldly outcome was discussed in Al Imran, while his hereafter is the Fire.
rows.anchor: أي ضن بما عنده ، فلم يبذل خيرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن الضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by al-Dahhak, explains the hard course as God preventing the person from believing in God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس " فسنيسره للعسرى " قال : سوف أحول بينه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وعنه عن ابن عباس قال : نزلت في أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Ikrima, explains that the person hoarded his wealth and considered himself independent of his Lord.
rows.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس : " وأما من بخل واستغنى " يقول : بخل بماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi glosses denying the good as denying God's promised recompense for giving.
rows.anchor: " وكذب بالحسنى " أي بالخلف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, in Ibn Abi Najih's transmission, interprets the good as Paradise.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد : " وكذب بالحسن " قال : بالجنة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In another transmission from Mujahid, the good means the testimony that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: وبإسناد عنه آخر قال " بالحسنى " أي بلا إله إلا اللّه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God will make the person's path easy.
rows.anchor: " فسنيسره " أي نسهل طريقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hard course means evil.
rows.anchor: " للعسرى " أي للشر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud interprets the hard course as the Fire.
rows.anchor: أي للشر . وعن ابن مسعود : للنار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God makes the causes of good and righteousness difficult for him, so acting on them becomes hard.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أي فسنعسر عليه أسباب الخير والصلاح حتى يصعب عليه فعلها

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi recalls Abu al-Darda's report of angels calling morning and evening for recompense for the spender and loss for the miser.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم أن الملك ينادي صباحا ومساء : [ اللهم أعط منفقا خلفا ، وأعط ممسكا تلفا ] . رواه أبو الدرداء

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars infer from this and other verses that generosity is a noble virtue and miserliness a vile one.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء : ثبت بهذه الآية وبقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Generosity means giving where giving is proper; miserliness means withholding where giving is due, not giving indiscriminately or withholding where restraint is proper.
rows.anchor: وليس الجواد الذي يعطي في غير موضع العطاء ، ولا البخيل الذي يمنع في موضع المنع ، لكن الجواد الذي يعطي في موضع العطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving that earns no reward or praise but merits blame is wasteful, not generosity; such spendthrifts are described as Satan's brothers and are subject to interdiction.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يستفد بالعطاء أجرا ولا حمدا ، وإنما استوجب به ذما فليس بجواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person whose withholding merits neither blame nor punishment but earns praise is rightly guided and fit to manage others' wealth because of sound judgment.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يستوجب بالمنع عقابا ولا ذما ، واستوجب به حمدا ، فهو من أهل الرشد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra answers the apparent paradox of making someone easy for hardship by analogy to giving glad tidings of painful punishment: paired good and evil statements use the same terms.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : يقول القائل : كيف قال : " فسنيسره للعسرى " ؟ وهل في العسرى تيسير ؟

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra glosses the verb as preparing someone; Arabs use it of sheep when they give birth or are ready to do so.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : وقوله تعالى : " فسنيسره " : سنهيئه . والعرب تقول : قد يسرت الغنم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: A cited poem uses the verb of ewes being ready to give birth, supporting al-Farra's explanation of preparing.
rows.anchor: هما سيدانا يزعمان وإنما *** يسوداننا أن يسرت غنماهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the phrase can mean when the person dies, perishes, falls into Hell, or goes away; the verb also describes falling into a well or plunging from a mountain.
rows.anchor: ويقال : ردي في البئر وتردى : إذا سقط في بئر ، أو تهور من جبل

words: وَمَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥٓ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle may be negative: his wealth will not benefit him at all when he perishes.
rows.anchor: و " ما " : يحتمل أن تكون جحدا ، أي ولا يغني عنه ماله شيئا

words: وَمَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥٓ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the particle is an interrogative of rebuke: what could his wealth benefit him when he dies and falls into Hell?
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون استفهاما معناه التوبيخ ؛ أي أي شيء يغني عنه إذا هلك ووقع في جهنم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says guidance here means making the path of guidance distinct from the path of error, that is, clarifying the rulings.
rows.anchor: فالهدى : بمعنى بيان الأحكام ، قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada specifies that God clarifies what is lawful and forbidden, and what constitutes obedience and disobedience.
rows.anchor: بيان حلال وحرامه ، وطاعته ومعصيته . قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says that whoever follows guidance is on God's path, citing the verse that God's responsibility is the directed path.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : من سلك الهدى فعلى اللّه سبيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading includes both guidance and misguidance, with the latter omitted, as in verses that mention one side while implying its counterpart.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معناه إن علينا للهدى والإضلال ، فترك الإضلال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God undertakes the reward of the guidance He has given.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أي إن علينا ثواب هداه الذي هديناه

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas interpreting the hereafter as Paradise and the first life as this world.
rows.anchor: " للآخرة " الجنة . " والأولى " الدنيا . وكذا روى عطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi concludes that both this world and the hereafter belong to God.
rows.anchor: أي الدنيا والآخرة{[16119]} لله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih reports Ibn Abbas interpreting the phrase as the rewards of this world and the hereafter; whoever seeks them from anyone but their owner has taken the wrong path.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال : ثواب الدنيا والآخرة ، وهو كقوله تعالى : " من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To undergo the Fire means to experience its heat.
rows.anchor: " لا يصلاها " أي لا يجد صلاها وهو حرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched one means the wretched person.
rows.anchor: " إلا الأشقى " أي الشقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who denied is the Prophet Muhammad's message, and turning away means turning away from faith.
rows.anchor: " الذي كذب " نبي اللّه محمدا صلى اللّه عليه وسلم . " وتولى " أي أعرض عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that everyone enters Paradise except whoever refuses it; he identifies the refuser as the one who denied and turned away.
rows.anchor: وروى مكحول عن أبي هريرة قال : كل يدخل الجنة إلا من أباها

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik recounts Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz crying so hard at the warning of blazing Fire during Maghrib prayer that he could not continue the sura and read another.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك : صلى بنا عمر بن عبد العزيز المغرب ، فقرأ " والليل إذا يغشى "

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the wretched one is whoever was wretched in God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: إلا من كان شقيا في علم اللّه جل ثناؤه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن الضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, identifies the wretched one with Umayya ibn Khalaf and those like him who denied Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : " لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى " أمية بن خلف ونظراؤه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says he denied God's Book and turned away from obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : كذب بكتاب اللّه ، وتولى عن طاعة اللّه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says this need not mean explicit denial: falling short of commanded obedience is called denial, like facing an enemy and then retreating.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : لم يكن كذب برد ظاهر ، ولكنه قصر عما أمر به من الطاعة ، فجعل تكذيبا

rows.speaker: أبو ثروان
rows.claim: Abu Tharwan's idiom about Banu Numayr says their forebear has no retreat in him, meaning they fight truthfully and do not turn back.
rows.anchor: وسمعت أبا ثروان يقول : إن بني نمير

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra connects the same usage to the verse saying the Hour's arrival has no falsehood, meaning it is certainly true.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله جل ثناؤه :  " ليس لوقعتها

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the Murji'a use these verses to argue that only unbelievers enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا إسحاق الزجاج يقول

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects that inference: this is a particular Fire, while Hell has levels, including the hypocrites' lowest level, and God may punish with any threatened kind of torment.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا إسحاق الزجاج يقول

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj adds that God forgives sins short of associating partners for whomever He wills; otherwise that promise would have no meaning, so non-polytheists may still be punished.
rows.anchor: وقال جل ثناؤه :  " إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari sees a contrast between exemplary leaders among unbelievers and believers: each is described in the superlative as if the Fire or Garden were made for him alone.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري : الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported identification names Abu Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf as the wretched figure and Abu Bakr as the God-fearing figure.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف . وأبو بكر رضي اللّه عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To be kept away from the Fire means to be distant from it.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " وسيجنبها " أي يكون بعيدا منها . " الأتقى " أي المتقي الخائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most God-fearing means the person who is pious and fearful.
rows.anchor: " الأتقى " أي المتقي الخائف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the God-fearing one as Abu Bakr, who is kept from entering the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هو أبو بكر رضي اللّه عنه ، يزحزح عن دخول النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing person gives wealth seeking purity with God and His approval, without ostentation or desire for reputation.
rows.anchor: ثم وصف الأتقى فقال : " الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى " أي يطلب أن يكون عند اللّه زاكيا

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Some semanticists say the forms atqa and ashqa mean pious and wretched; the Afʿal pattern can stand for faʿil, as in akbar meaning kabir and ahwan meaning hayyin, with Tarafa's poem illustrating the usage.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني : أراد بقوله " الأتقى " و " الأشقى " أي التقي والشقي ، كقول طرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is Meccan by agreement and has eleven verses.
rows.anchor: مكية باتفاق . وهي إحدى عشرة آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forenoon means daytime, paired with night as its opposite; the usage is like the verse describing people playing by day.
rows.anchor: قد تقدم القول في " الضحى " ، والمراد به النهار ؛ لقوله : " والليل إذا سجى " فقابله بالليل

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل وجعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Qatada, Muqatil, and Ja'far al-Sadiq say God swears by the forenoon when He spoke to Moses and by the night of the Ascension.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل وجعفر الصادق : أقسم بالضحى الذي كلم اللّه فيه موسى ، وبليلة المعراج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the forenoon as the hour when the sorcerers fell prostrate, supported by the verse about gathering the people at forenoon.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي الساعة التي خر فيها السحرة سجدا

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: People of rhetoric say the oath has an ellipsis: its sense is by the Lord of the forenoon.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني فيه وفي أمثاله : فيه إضمار ، مجازه ورب الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best-known linguistic meaning of saja is becoming still, as when people settle during the night; stillness can also mean its darkness settling and becoming even.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أشهر في اللغة : " سجا " سكن ، أي سكن الناس فيه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss explains the night's stillness as its darkness becoming settled and even.
rows.anchor: وقيل : سكونه استقرار ظلامه واستواؤه

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-A'sha's line calls the sea calm with saja, supporting the sense of stillness.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى : فما ذنبنا{[16133]} أن جاش بحر ابن عمكم *** وبحرك ساج

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz line describes a calm night, using saj to mean still.
rows.anchor: وقال الراجز : يا حبذا القمراء والليل الساج *** وطرق مثل ملاء النساج

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir's verse calls eyes سواجي, using the same root for still eyes.
rows.anchor: وقال جرير : ولقد رمينك يوم رحن بأعين *** ينظرن من خلل الستور سواجي

rows.speaker: الضحاك والأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says saja means covering everything; al-Asma'i explains the night covering daytime as a person is covered by a cloth.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك :  " سجا " غطى كل شيء . قال الأصمعي : سجو الليل : تغطيته النهار

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Abbas say the night covers everything with its darkness.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : غشى بظلامه . وقاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses saja as the night departing, and elsewhere as its becoming dark.
rows.anchor: وعنه : إذا ذهب . وعنه أيضا : إذا أظلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and a report from Qatada take saja to mean that night approached.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : أقبل ، وروي عن قتادة أيضا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, in Ibn Abi Najih's transmission, says saja means becoming even or settled.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد : " سجا " استوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the two oaths as God's servants who worship at forenoon and those who worship at nightfall.
rows.anchor: عباده الذين يعبدونه في وقت الضحى ، وعباده الذين يعبدونه بالليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the forenoon the light of Paradise when it shines and the night the darkness when it darkens.
rows.anchor: ويقال : " الضحى " : يعني نور الجنة إذا تنور . " والليل إذا سجا " : يعني ظلمة الليل إذا أظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inward interpretation makes the forenoon the light in the hearts of the knowers and the night the darkness in the hearts of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ويقال : " والضحى " : يعني النور الذي في قلوب العارفين كهيئة النهار . " والليل إذا سجا " : يعني السواد الذي في قلوب الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recalls His favor: Muhammad's father had died, and God sheltered and supported him through his uncle Abu Talib.
rows.anchor: عدد سبحانه مننه على نبيه محمد صلى اللّه عليه وسلم فقال : " ألم يجدك يتيما " لا أب لك قد مات أبوك . " فآوى " أي جعل لك مأوى

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
rows.claim: Ja'far al-Sadiq answers that the Prophet was orphaned from both parents so that no created being would have a claim over him.
rows.anchor: وقيل لجعفر بن محمد الصادق : لم أوتم النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم من أبويه ؟ فقال : لئلا يكون لمخلوق عليه حق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid notes that Arabs call a pearl yatim when it has no equal; metaphorically, God found Muhammad unmatched in nobility and gave him protective companions.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : هو من قول العرب : درة يتيمة ، إذا لم يكن لها مثل . فمجاز الآية : ألم يجدك واحدا في شرفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi first explains the phrase as Muhammad being unaware of what prophethood meant for him, then God guiding him; here error means heedlessness, as in verses about God not being heedless and Muhammad once being among the heedless.
rows.anchor: أي غافلا عما يراد بك من أمر النبوة ، فهداك : أي أرشدك . والضلال هنا بمعنى الغفلة

rows.speaker: الضحاك وشهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak, Shahr ibn Hawshab, and others say he did not know the Qur'an or religious law, and God guided him to them, as in 42:52.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم : " ضالا " لم تكن تدري القرآن والشرائع ، فهداك اللّه إلى القرآن ، وشرائع الإسلام ، عن الضحاك وشهر بن حوشب وغيرهما

rows.speaker: الكلبي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and al-Farra say he was among a misguided people and God guided them through him.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم : " ووجدك ضالا " أي في قوم ضلال ، فهداهم اللّه بك . هذا قول الكلبي والفراء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi gives a similar sense: Muhammad's people were astray, and God guided him to show them the way.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي نحوه ، أي ووجد قومك في ضلال ، فهداك إلى إرشادهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God found him seeking the migration and guided him to it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : " ووجدك ضالا " عن الهجرة ، فهداك إليها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God reminded him to make an exception when asked about the People of the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit, as in the verse about one of two women erring.
rows.anchor: وقيل : " ضالا " أي ناسيا شأن الاستثناء حين سئلت عن أصحاب الكهف وذي القرنين والروح – فأذكرك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says he was seeking the direction of prayer and God guided him to it, citing the turning of his face toward heaven.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ووجدك طالبا للقبلة فهداك إليها . بيانه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation makes him perplexed about explaining what had been revealed, then guided to its explanation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ووجدك متحيرا عن بيان ما نزل عليك ، فهداك إليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says he was lost or obscure among his people, and God guided him to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ووجدك ضائعا في قومك ، فهداك إليه

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق وغيره
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq and others say he loved Abu Talib and God guided him to love his Lord.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق وغيره : " ووجدك ضالا " : تحب أبا طالب ، فهداك إلى محبة ربك

rows.speaker: بسّام بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Bassam ibn Abd Allah says he was unaware of himself, and God made him know himself and his state.
rows.anchor: وقال بسام بن عبد الله : " ووجدك ضالا " بنفسك لا تدري من أنت ، فعرفك بنفسك وحالك

rows.speaker: الجنيدي
rows.claim: Al-Junayd says he was perplexed about explaining the Book, so God taught him its exposition, as in verses assigning the Prophet to explain revelation and disputes.
rows.anchor: وقال الجنيدي : ووجدك متحيرا في بيان الكتاب ، فعلمك البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some theologians say Arabs call a solitary tree in a wasteland a dallah because travelers use it to find the way; al-Qurtubi prefers this as it gathers the figurative readings: Muhammad stood alone in his religion and God guided creation through him.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المتكلمين : إذا وجدت العرب شجرة منفردة في فلاة من الأرض ، لا شجر معها ، سموها ضالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the solitary-tree interpretation is most appealing because it gathers the figurative interpretations of the verse.
rows.anchor: قلت : هذه الأقوال كلها حسان ، ثم منها ما هو معنوي ، ومنها ما هو حسي . والقول الأخير أعجب إلي

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say he outwardly followed the general customs of his people for forty years without openly opposing them, while shirk should not be attributed to him.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم : إنه كان على جملة ما كان القوم عليه ، لا يظهر لهم خلافا على ظاهر الحال ، فأما الشرك فلا يظن به

rows.speaker: الكلبي والسدي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and al-Suddi take the phrase literally as saying he was an unbeliever with an unbelieving people; al-Qurtubi points back to its rebuttal in Surat al-Shura.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي والسدي : هذا على ظاهره ، أي وجدك كافرا والقوم كفار فهداك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says he already treated and refuted this attribution in Surat al-Shura.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى هذا القول والرد عليه في سورة " الشورى "

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says he was immersed among the people of shirk and God distinguished him from them, like water lost within milk.
rows.anchor: وقيل : وجدك مغمورا بأهل الشرك ، فميزك عنهم . يقال : ضل الماء في اللبن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes dalal to mean love: God found him loving guidance and led him to it; the word is used for love in the cited verse and poetry.
rows.anchor: ويكون الضلال بمعنى المحبة . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An anonymous poet uses dalal in the sense of love, supporting this lexical interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : هذا الضلال أشاب مني المفرقا *** والعارضين ولم أكن متحققا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan's explanatory reading has the straying one become guided through the Prophet: God found the lost one and he was guided by you.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة الحسن " ووجدك ضال فهدى " أي وجدك الضال فاهتدى بك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A final view says his people did not know his worth, so God guided Muslims to him until they believed in him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : " ووجدك ضالا " لا يهتدي إليك قومك ، ولا يعرفون قدرك ، فهدى المسلمين إليك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that Muhammad was lost in Mecca's ravines as a child; Abu Jahl found him away from his sheep and returned him to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ضل النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم وهو صغير في شعاب مكة ، فرآه أبو جهل منصرفا عن أغنامه ، فرده إلى جده عبدالمطلب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr recounts that Satan diverted the Prophet's camel from the road during a dark journey with Abu Talib, until Gabriel cast Satan away to India and returned the Prophet to the caravan.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : خرج النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم مع عمه أبي طالب في سفر ، فأخذ إبليس بزمام الناقة في ليلة ظلماء

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b tells how Halima's infant Muhammad disappeared as she returned him to Mecca; signs at the idols and a heavenly voice led Abd al-Muttalib to find him beneath a tree.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب : إن حليمة لما قضت حق الرضاع ، جاءت برسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم لترده على عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view places this guidance on the night of the Ascension, when Gabriel left him and God guided him to the base of the Throne.
rows.anchor: وقيل : " ووجدك ضالا " ليلة المعراج ، حين انصرف عنك جبريل وأنت لا تعرف الطريق ، فهداك إلى ساق العرش
